h1: J&Y Lodge Hotel — a budget hotel in Amata Nakorn, just three minutes from the estate
intro: Picture this: you clock off at Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate and you're at your hotel within a few minutes, parking for free out front, then walking over to grab dinner at Ninja Market Amata just three hundred-odd metres away — J&Y Lodge Hotel is a 3-star budget hotel in the Amata Nakorn area of Nong Mai Daeng, Mueang Chon Buri district, sitting right next to Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate, about 3 min away by car, and about 8 min from Chonburi Hospital · What most people bring up is the affordable price and how close it is to the estate, which suits people working in the industrial zone and anyone after a cheap overnight stop · It has 146 rooms in total, each around 28 sqm, starting at about THB 650/night, with an overall score of about 7.6 from 537 reviews on Agoda and SHA Plus certification

body.html: Overview and who it suits — To put it as simply as possible, J&Y Lodge Hotel is a hotel for people who want a clean, simple, affordable place to stay in the Amata Nakorn area of Mueang Chon Buri, rather than anyone hunting for a beachfront resort or a luxury stay in a tourist district · It's a 3-star hotel that has been open since around 2012, located in Nong Mai Daeng, Mueang Chon Buri district, in a zone surrounded by industrial estates, factories and worker housing · With around 146 rooms and a concept built on value for money, the real reviews line up on this point: the people it suits best are those coming to work or run errands at Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate and the Chonburi industrial zone — company staff, engineers, technicians coming in for stretches at a time, and people posted here short- to medium-term · Another group who say it's worth it are those driving the Chonburi route who want a cheap overnight stop with parking and easy access, plus people visiting nearby Chonburi Hospital · On the flip side, anyone set on a trip to Bang Saen beach or Pattaya, or looking for a resort feel with full facilities like a pool, may find the location and style here don't match what they want, and should look at stays in Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · Put simply, J&Y Lodge plays on "value and close to the estate" first and foremost, rather than selling sea views or a holiday mood

Location and getting around — The location of J&Y Lodge is both a strength and something to understand correctly before you book · The hotel is at 479/19 Moo 1, Nong Mai Daeng, Mueang Chon Buri district, only about 3 min by car from Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate (Amata City Chonburi), which is the main selling point for anyone heading in and out of the estate every day · It's about 8 min from Chonburi Hospital, so people coming to visit or sit with a patient can stay conveniently too · The nearby spot reviews mention most is Ninja Market Amata, only about 320 m away — a night market with food and goods to browse every evening — plus the Institute of Physical Education sports ground about 490 m away and several local restaurants around the hotel · As for popular attractions, Bang Saen beach is a fair drive away, while Chonburi railway station is about 15 km away and Suvarnabhumi Airport about 51 km · The honest note from the reviews is that this place is most convenient when you have your own car, because the Nong Mai Daeng–Amata Nakorn area is an estate-and-housing zone where public transport isn't as dense as in town · The upside is the hotel has free parking and a taxi-booking service you can ask about · In short, if you have a car this location is very handy for estate errands and passing through, but without one you should plan ahead for transport and book a ride in advance

"An easy stay close to work in the estate, cheap, rooms clean enough, parking is easy, and you can walk to Ninja Market for dinner in the evening · For anyone working around Amata Nakorn who wants to save, this hits the right note on location and price"

Room types and decor — J&Y Lodge has 146 rooms in total, all similar in size at around 28 sqm, which counts as fairly roomy for a budget hotel in this area · They're divided mainly by bed configuration: the Deluxe Room, where you can choose between one queen bed or two single beds; the Deluxe Twin Room with two single beds for friends or colleagues travelling together; the Deluxe Double Room with a queen bed for solo travellers or couples; and the Budget Twin Room, the most economical option · The decor is simple and practical with an easy-on-the-eye tone, every room air-conditioned with a flat-screen TV, an en-suite bathroom and Wi-Fi · Most real reviews rate cleanliness as good (around 8.4 out of 10 on some platforms) and say the rooms are cleaner and roomier than expected for the price · But to be straight about it, this hotel has been open since around 2012, so some reviews note that the decor and certain fittings are starting to show their age, and the upkeep isn't consistent across every room — some rooms come in better shape than others · If quietness matters to you, ask for a room away from the main road or common areas right at booking, and if you get a room that isn't in the condition you want, flag it straight away to swap, because with a fairly large number of rooms there's usually one to switch to

Facilities — It has to be said up front that J&Y Lodge is a budget hotel built on simplicity, with no swimming pool and no resort-style fitness centre, so if you're after a stay with full leisure facilities, this place may not match what you want · But in terms of what you actually need for a stay, the hotel provides enough: free Wi-Fi in the common areas, free parking, an on-site restaurant, a garden and terrace, an elevator, an ATM, a taxi-booking service, luggage storage and a clothes dryer · The front desk is open 24 hours, so anyone working shifts or arriving late can check in easily · For estate workers, having free parking and an on-site restaurant makes daily life easier without having to head out often, and with Ninja Market Amata within walking distance, food and daily essentials aren't a problem · Overall the facilities here sit at the "right for the price" level — everything you need for a working stay or an overnight stop, but without the leisure extras you'd get from a higher-tier hotel, which is something to set your expectations on before you book

Food and dining — J&Y Lodge has an on-site restaurant that serves a la carte breakfast from around 6:30 AM–10:00 AM — dishes ordered to order rather than a big buffet like a higher-tier hotel — good for anyone who wants a simple morning meal before heading to work · Being a budget hotel, the in-house food options aren't as varied as at a big hotel, but the location helps a lot, because there are several local restaurants around the hotel and Ninja Market Amata, only about 320 m away, is the evening food spot many reviews bring up — rice dishes, fried snacks, desserts and drinks at local prices · So many people choose to eat out rather than rely on the hotel restaurant for every meal, which fits a style of stay that uses the hotel as a base to sleep and then heads out for food in the area · For workers who have to start early, having an in-house spot that begins serving at 6:30 AM means no trekking far for breakfast · Overall, food isn't the reason to come to J&Y Lodge to eat in-house, but it's an adequate add-on for breakfast, with the market and local restaurants around it covering the rest of your meals

Service — Service at J&Y Lodge scores in the okay-to-good range in real reviews, sitting at around 7.8 out of 10 on some platforms · Many say the staff are friendly and helpful in the way of a local hotel, and the 24-hour front desk makes check-in and check-out flexible, which suits shift workers on irregular hours · Services that make the stay easier include the taxi-booking service, luggage storage and help with parking · But to be straight about it, being a budget hotel with a small team, some reviews say the care and responsiveness aren't equally consistent at all times, and the service standard depends on the time of day and how busy it is with guests · This is common for hotels at this price point, and overall the service still counts as acceptable for what you pay, especially compared with what you'd expect from a 3-star hotel in an estate area

What real reviews say (the good and the bad) — Pulling together Agoda, Trip.com and Booking.com, the picture has points that line up and points that differ by platform · On the praise side: cheap and good value for a simple stay, a location near Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate that's very handy for workers, cleanliness in the good range (some platforms rate cleanliness around 8.4), rooms roomy enough at around 28 sqm, free parking, and being near Ninja Market Amata within walking distance for food · On the watch-out side: the honest thing to say is that review scores vary widely by platform — Agoda gives about 7.6 from a large sample of 537 reviews, while Booking.com gives only about 5.6 from a small sample of just 6 reviews, and Tripadvisor ranks it fairly low in the table · This gap reflects that the experience can be inconsistent — some are very satisfied while others are disappointed · The criticisms include inconsistent upkeep and room condition in line with the age of a building open since around 2012, the lack of a pool and leisure facilities, and a location that isn't convenient for those without a car · Most of these criticisms are things you can manage by setting your expectations to match the price and choosing your room, rather than major problems for anyone who just wants a cheap stay near the estate

"Cheap, rooms clean enough, free parking is reassuring, and you can walk to Ninja Market · The only knock is the building's starting to age and there's no pool, but if you're here on a budget for work in the estate it's fine at this price"

Price comparison and value — Nightly rates start at about THB 650/night for a Budget or Deluxe room at standard prices, climbing to around THB 800–THB 1,100 when there's an event at the estate or over a long weekend · What makes J&Y Lodge good value is that you get an air-conditioned room of around 28 sqm that's clean enough, with free parking and a location just 3 min from Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate, at a price in the hundreds to low thousands of baht, which counts as easy to reach for workers and regular guests · Compared with a Japanese-themed hotel with an onsen like J Park Hotel in the same area, which starts at around THB 1,000 and up and has a pool and onsen, J&Y Lodge is cheaper but clearly offers fewer facilities · And compared with stays in Bang Saen or Pattaya, those win on sea views and a holiday mood, while J&Y Lodge wins on price and being close to the estate · In short, if you weight affordable price and a location near work in the estate most heavily, this place delivers value that fits the group, but if you want leisure facilities or a holiday atmosphere, add to your budget and look at options that offer more

What to know before you book — There are several things that make the stay smoother · One, the location is in an estate-and-housing area, most convenient when you have your own car; without one, plan ahead to book a ride or use the hotel's taxi-booking service, and use the free parking if you drive yourself · Two, there's no pool and no leisure facilities here, so set your expectations correctly that this is a budget hotel for sleeping and working, not a holiday stay · Three, with review scores varying widely by platform, it's worth reading recent reviews from several sources before deciding, and if you get a room that isn't in the condition you expected, flag it to the front desk straight away to swap · Four, the front desk is open 24 hours and the restaurant starts serving breakfast from 6:30 AM, which suits people starting early at the estate or arriving late · Five, a deposit of around THB 500 is collected at check-in and refunded at check-out, and there's an extra bed available for a fee, so ask ahead if you're coming as a family · Six, when there's a trade show or event at Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate, rooms tend to fill up fast, so book ahead, compare prices across several platforms, and choose a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't firm yet

The verdict — From all the real reviews, J&Y Lodge Hotel is the best fit for people working or running errands at Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate and the Chonburi industrial zone, as well as anyone wanting an affordable place for an overnight stop or a regular stay · A location just 3 min from Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate, close to Chonburi Hospital, and within walking distance of Ninja Market Amata, plus free parking and rates starting in the hundreds of baht, make it line up well on value and convenience for this group · Rooms that are roomy enough at around 28 sqm and cleanliness in the good range according to reviews are what help keep the Agoda score at around 7.6 · But it has to be acknowledged that this is a budget hotel with no pool or leisure facilities, the building is starting to age in line with having opened around 2012, the upkeep isn't consistent in some spots, and review scores vary widely by platform enough that you should read several sources before deciding · If you're looking for a beachfront stay in a tourist district or want full facilities, this isn't the answer, and you should look at options in Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · But for a work trip, an overnight stop near Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate, or a budget stay built around location and price — J&Y Lodge meets that need in a way that's honest and worth the money

faq.q: Where is J&Y Lodge Hotel Chonburi · is it easy to get to?
faq.a: The hotel is at 479/19 Moo 1, Nong Mai Daeng, Mueang Chon Buri district, in the Amata Nakorn area · About 3 min by car from Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate and about 8 min from Chonburi Hospital · Walk to Ninja Market Amata (~320 m) · About 15 km from Chonburi railway station and about 51 km from Suvarnabhumi Airport · This area is most convenient when you have your own car, with free parking; without one, plan ahead to book a ride or use the hotel's taxi-booking service

faq.q: Does J&Y Lodge Hotel have a pool · what facilities are there?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool, as it's a budget hotel built on simplicity · The facilities include free Wi-Fi, free parking, an on-site restaurant, a garden and terrace, an elevator, an ATM, a taxi-booking service and luggage storage · The front desk is open 24 hours, good for people working shifts or arriving late

faq.q: What's the starting price at J&Y Lodge Hotel · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 650/night for a Budget/Deluxe room at standard prices · Every room is around 28 sqm, with Budget Twin, Deluxe Double (queen bed), Deluxe Twin (2 single beds) and Deluxe Room with a choice of bed type · Rooms fill up fast during estate events, so compare several platforms before booking · A deposit of around THB 500 is collected at check-in and refunded at check-out

faq.q: Who does J&Y Lodge Hotel suit best?
faq.a: It's a great fit for people working or running errands at Amata Nakorn Industrial Estate and the Chonburi industrial zone, as well as anyone wanting a budget place for an overnight stop or a regular stay, and people visiting nearby Chonburi Hospital · It's not a fit for those set on a trip to Bang Saen beach or Pattaya, or wanting full facilities like a pool, who should look at Bang Saen or Pattaya instead

faq.q: What are the review scores for J&Y Lodge Hotel · how reliable are they?
faq.a: The scores vary widely by platform — Agoda gives about 7.6 from a large sample of 537 reviews, while Booking.com gives about 5.6 from just 6 reviews, and Trip.com sits at around 7.4 · This gap reflects that the experience can be inconsistent · It's worth reading recent reviews from several sources before deciding and setting your expectations to match the affordable price

faq.q: What are the food and cleanliness like at J&Y Lodge Hotel?
faq.a: There's an on-site restaurant serving a la carte breakfast around 6:30 AM–10:00 AM · In-house options aren't very varied, but there are local restaurants around and Ninja Market Amata within walking distance · On cleanliness, most reviews rate it good (around 8.4 on some platforms), saying the rooms are clean and roomy enough · But the building has been open since around 2012, so some spots are starting to age and the upkeep isn't consistent across every room; if a room isn't as expected, flag it to the front desk straight away to swap
